text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes is diagnosed using specific blood tests ordered by a healthcare provider, as outlined by the Mayo Clinic and MedlinePlus.
snippet_highlighted_words: using specific blood tests ordered by a healthcare provider

list.snippet: Hemoglobin A1C Test: Measures your average blood sugar level over the past 2 to 3 months.
Diabetes range: 6.5% or higher on two separate tests.
Fasting Plasma Glucose (FPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar after you fast (not eating or drinking anything except water) for at least 8 hours.
Diabetes range: 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher.
Prediabetes range: 100 to 125 mg/dL (5.6 to 6.9 mmol/L).
Random Plasma Glucose (RPG) Test: Measures your blood sugar at any time of day, regardless of when you last ate.
Diabetes range: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher, usually paired with classic diabetes symptoms like extreme thirst, frequent urination, or unexplained weight loss.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Measures your blood sugar before and 2 hours after you drink a special sugary liquid.
Diabetes range: 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher at the 2-hour mark.
Repeat Testing: Except in cases of clear symptoms with a high random glucose test, doctors usually confirm a diabetes diagnosis by repeating one of the tests on a different day.
Risk Assessment: You can take a quick self-assessment using the ADA Risk Test to evaluate your personal risk factors.
